US-WV.note: West Virginia has no statewide rent limit and no statute barring local rent limits, and it is not treated as a Dillon's Rule state (§ 8-1-7 drops strict construction) because every municipality has plenary power to promote public welfare and good order (§ 8-12-5(43)), so a city could probably act; this is untested, and § 8-1-5a(k), which bars municipalities from prohibiting or effectively limiting the rental of property, could be read against it.

US-NH.cite: N.H. RSA 31:39; RSA 47:17 (enumerated bylaw powers; no grant over rents); RSA 540, 540-A (no rent-limit provision)
US-NH.note: Weak: no New Hampshire statute bars local rent limits, but New Hampshire follows Dillon's Rule and neither the town bylaw list (RSA 31:39) nor the city bylaw list (RSA 47:17) grants power over rents, so cities and towns cannot act.
